newsitem.title: SYRIA: Syria says will try other means if peace fails.
newsitem.headline: Syria says will try other means if peace fails.

text.p: Syria warned Israel on Wednesday it would try other ways of winning back the Golan Heights captured by the Jewish state in 1967 if the Middle East peace process failed.

Tawfiq Salhah, a member of the regional command of Syria's Baath ruling party, told a conference of Syria's communist party that Damascus was still committed to peace but would not wait long to liberate its lands.

"Syria will not accept the continuation of the occupation of its territories if the peace process fails. It will liberate the land with the method if finds appropriate and will be ready to confront any consequences," Salhah said.
The regional command is the highest party body which sets the country's internal and foreign policies.
Syria had strongly condemned Israeli Prime Minister Benjamin Netanyahu's refusal to trade occupied Arab lands for peace, the basis on which the 1991 peace process was built.
No talks have been held between Israel and Syria since Netanyahu took office in June and Damascus says it will not return to the negotiating table until Israel agrees to pull back from the Golan.

Syria and Israel traded accusations in recent weeks that each was preparing to launch a war against the other. Both conducted military exercises and redeployed some of their forces confronting each other but they said the moves were routine.
Salhah said Damascus would not accept an Israeli-style peace.

"Israel wants Arabs to capitulate and accept the peace it wants, the peace which achieves its strategic goals and allows it to materialize its dreams of greater Israel. But this will not happen...," Salhah said.
"Israel through its new government (of Netanyahu) is threatening and beating the drums of war. Israel should be responsible for the serious consequences of its arrogance... .," Salhah said.
